<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" />{{rh|102|THE GOSPEL|CHA. VI.}}</noinclude>{{hwe|rodias|Herodias}} came in, and had daunced, and pleased Herod, and them that sate vvith him at the table: the King said to the damsel, Aske of me vvhat thou vvilt, and I vvil giue it thee. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=23}}† and he svvare to her, That vvhatsoeuer thou shalt aske I vvil giue thee, though the halfe of my kingdom. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=24}}† Who vvhen she vvas gone forth, said to her mother, What shal I aske? But she said, The head of Iohn the Baptist. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=25}}† And vvhen she vvas gone in by and by vvith hast to the King, she asketh saying, I vvil that forthvvith thou giue me in a platter the head of Iohn the Baptist. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=26}}† And the King vvas stroken sad. Because of his othe and for them that sate together at table he vvould not displease her: {{verse|chapter=6|verse=27}}† but sending the hangman, commaunded that his head should be brought in a platter. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=28}}† And he beheaded him in the prison, and brought his head in a platter: and gaue it to the damsel, and the damsel gaue it to her mother. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=29}}† Which his disciples hearing came, and tooke his body: and they put it in a monument.⊣

{{verse|chapter=6|verse=30}}† And {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Lu. 9, 10.''}}* the Apostles gathering together vnto Iesus, made relation to him of al things that they had done and taught. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=31}}† And he said to them, Come apart into the desert place, and rest a litle. For there vvere that came and vvent, many: and they had not so much as space to eate. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=32}}† And {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Mt. 14, 13.''}}* going vp into the boate, they vvent into a desert place apart. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=33}}† And they savv them going avvay, and many knevv: and they ranne flocking thither on foote from al cities, and preuented them.

{{verse|chapter=6|verse=34}}† And going forth, {{sc|Iesvs}} savv a great multitude: and he had compassion on them, because they vvere as sheepe not hauing a shepheard, and he began to teach them many things. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=35}}† And {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Mt. 14, 15. Lu. 9, 12. Io. 6, 5.''}}* vvhen the day vvas novv farre spent, his Disciples came to him, saying, This is a desert place, and the houre is novv past: {{verse|chapter=6|verse=36}}† dimisse them, that going out into the next villages and tovvnes, they may bie them selues meates to eate. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=37}}† And he ansvvering said, Giue ye them to eate. And they said to him, Let vs goe and bie bread for tvvo hundred pence: and vve vvil giue them to eate. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=38}}† And he saith to them, Hovv many loaues haue you? goe and see. And vvhen they knevv, they say, Fiue, and tvvo fishes. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=39}}† And he commaunded them that they should make al sit dovvne, by companies vpon the greene grasse. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=40}}† And they sate dovvne in rankes by hundreds and fifties. {{verse|chapter=6|verse=41}}† And vvhen he had taken the fiue loaues, and the tvvo fishes: looking vp vnto heauen,<noinclude>{{rh|||he}}</noinclude>
